questions.stem: Suppose the university newspaper is inviting submissions from the students for its coming edition on a campus event that has impressed them most. You are now to write an essay for submission. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
Among all the campus events I have taken part in, a volunteer teaching trip impressed me the most. It was last autumn that I joined our university volunteer team and traveled to a small rural primary school.

I still remember the moment when I walked into that simple classroom and began my first English lesson. The children sat straight, their eyes shining with curiosity, and they repeated every new word after me as loudly as they could. When the bell rang, instead of running out to play, they crowded around my desk, asking how to pronounce the words on their notebooks. At that moment, I felt truly needed for the first time, and a warm sense of responsibility rose in my heart.

This experience taught me that knowledge is not only something for exams, but also a light that can warm and guide others. That is exactly why this volunteer trip remains the campus event that touches me most.

sections.title: Section II Listening Comprehension
sections.note: 听力为历年真题原文，题目与答案为官方标准答案；在线音频由语音合成朗读原文，不是考场录音；换浏览器、换手机都能播。

transcript.text: 1 Have you noticed how similar you are to your friends?
It may be because your brains operate in harmony with each other.
We know that friends are more likely to be the same age, gender and ethnic background as each other.
Now it seems their brains are alike, too. 2 Researchers at the University of California scanned the brains of 42 classmates while they watched videos intended to provoke varying responses.
Some people might find a romantic scene touching, for instance, while others would feel it was embarrassing.
The activity of friends' brains was more similar than that of people who didn't know each other, particularly in regions involved in attention, emotion and language.
This similarity was strong enough that it could be used to predict whether two people were already friends or not.
The relationship probably goes two ways.
We are drawn to people who think like us; we then influence their thoughts over time, which may push their brain activity into more closely resembling our own.

questions.stem: What may be the reason that friends are similar to each other according to the recent research?

options.text: They are generally the same age.
They have the same ethnic background.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：It may be because your brains operate in harmony with each other.信号：因果信号 because 。录音开头先抛问句“有没有发现你和朋友很像“，紧接 It may be because your brains operate in harmony with each other —— b…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：录音确实念到 friends are more likely to be the same age，They are generally the same age. 正盗用了这个 same age。但这句前面有 We know that，是“早已知道的旧结论“，并非题干所问的“近期研究发现的相似原因“——原因落在大脑那句，不在同龄这句。 借用原文：the same age, gender and ethnic background
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：Their interests are quite similar. 听起来很合常识，但录音通篇没提“兴趣（interests）“相似，只说了年龄、性别、族裔背景与大脑。它靠的是考生“朋友兴趣相投“的生活常识，而非录音内容，属未提及。
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：They have the same ethnic background. 盗用了录音的 ethnic background。和 B 一样，这句出自 We know that friends are more likely to be the same age, gender and ethnic background，是“已知的旧情况“，不是近期研究新发现的相似原因，答非所问。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（your brains operate in harmony with each other ↔ Their brains work in harmony. operate 换说成 work）

questions.evidenceText: It may be because your brains operate in harmony with each other.

questions.stem: What does the news report say about the relationship between friends?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：The relationship probably goes two ways. We are drawn to people who think like us; we then influence their thoughts over time, which may push their brain activity into more closely resembling our own.信号：定性句 goes two ways 。录音第二段结尾用 The relationship probably goes two ways 直接给“关系“下定性，后面 We are drawn to people…; w…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：It can be touching. 盗用了录音的 touching，可那个 touching 出现在 Some people might find a romantic scene touching——是在举例说明“不同人对同一画面反应不同“，说的是“浪漫场景“感人，根本不是在评价“朋友关系“。张冠李戴，答非所问。 借用原文：it could be used to predict whether two people were already friends or not
optionAnalysis.B: 与原文相反：It is hard to predict. 借了录音的 predict。但录音说的是 it could be used to predict whether two people were already friends or not——意思是“大脑相似度高到能用来预测两人是不是朋友“，是说“能预测“，根本没说“关系难预测“。选项把“能预测“反着说成了“难预测“，与原文相反。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：It resembles family ties. 听着像那么回事，但录音全程没把朋友关系比作“家庭纽带（family ties）“，只说了关系“双向“。它纯靠考生自行联想，录音无任何对应，属未提及。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（The relationship probably goes two ways ↔ It can work both ways. two ways 换成 both ways）

questions.evidenceText: The relationship probably goes two ways. We are drawn to people who think like us; we then influence their thoughts over time, which may push their brain activity into more closely resembling our own.

transcript.text: 1 Two men who have been best friends for 60 years have just realized they are actually brothers.
It's reported that Alan Robinson and Walter MacDonald met in the 6th grade at a school in Hawaii.
They have been best friends ever since.
Alan was given away for adoption soon after he was born, and Walter never knew his father.
So recently, they made separate attempts on DNA matching websites to discover more about their ancestry.
Walter was astonished to find that he matched with website user Robi 737.
He knew immediately that this was his best friend Alan, whose friends call him Robi and flew 737 airplanes when he was a pilot.
The pair were born to the same mother 15 months apart.

questions.stem: What did both Alan Robinson and Walter MacDonald attempt to do on DNA matching websites?

options.text: Find out more about their ancestry.
See whether they are actually related.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：So recently, they made separate attempts on DNA matching websites to discover more about their ancestry.信号：题干原词attempt复现+目的句 。题干问 attempt to do，录音里恰好出现 made separate attempts on DNA matching websites，attempt 和 DNA m…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：A 说去 Search for their half-brothers.(寻找同父异母的兄弟)。录音确实出现 they are actually brothers‘他们其实是兄弟’，A 盗用了 brothers 这个词，但录音里这是新闻最后揭晓的真相，不是他俩上网时‘想去找的目标’——而且他们是同母兄弟、不是 half-brothers，张冠李戴。 借用原文：Walter never knew his father
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：B 说去 Identify their biological fathers.(确认亲生父亲)。录音有 Walter never knew his father，B 盗用了 father 一词，但这只是介绍背景，两人上网的目的写得很清楚是 discover more about their ancestry(查家世)，不是专门去认父亲。 借用原文：they are actually brothers
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：D 说去 See whether they are actually related.(看看俩人是否真有亲属关系)。录音里 they are actually brothers 用了 actually 一词，D 盗用了 actually 并改写成 related，可他们上网时压根不知道彼此有血缘、不是‘去验证是否有关系’，验出是兄弟是意外结果，不是上网动机。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（to discover more about their ancestry ↔ Find out more about their ancestry. discover换成find out，ancestry原样）

questions.evidenceText: So recently, they made separate attempts on DNA matching websites to discover more about their ancestry.

questions.stem: What did the news report say about Alan Robinson and Walter MacDonald?

options.text: They were both given up for adoption.
They were born to the same mother.
They were both 60 years of age.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：The pair were born to the same mother 15 months apart.信号：结尾收束句给出血缘真相 。新闻把最关键的血缘结论放在末句 The pair were born to the same mother 15 months apart——新闻报道常把核心事实或结局压在结尾，这个‘篇末收…

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：A 说两人 They were both given up for adoption.(都被送养)。录音里确有 Alan was given away for adoption，A 盗用了 adoption，但录音只说 Alan 一个人被送养，A 却说成 both(两个人都)，把范围从一人扩大到两人，与原文不符。 借用原文：flew 737 airplanes when he was a pilot
optionAnalysis.C: 张冠李戴：C 说两人 They flew 737 airplanes as pilots.(都当飞行员开737)。录音念到了 flew 737 airplanes when he was a pilot，C 盗用了 737 和 pilot 这两个醒目词，但 he 指的只是 Alan 一人，C 说成 They(两人都飞)，把一人之事安到两人头上。 借用原文：best friends for 60 years
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：D 说两人 They were both 60 years of age.(都60岁)。录音开头有 best friends for 60 years，D 盗用了数字 60，但这60是‘做了60年好朋友’，是友谊的年数，不是两人的年龄；偷换了60所修饰的对象。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（born to the same mother ↔ They were born to the same mother. 原句几乎照搬主语换成They）

questions.evidenceText: The pair were born to the same mother 15 months apart.

transcript.text: 1 Amid all the election drama, air pollution problems and disease outbreaks, five tourists' good work is being spread online.
Yesterday two male and three female tourists were spotted walking the kilometer-long beach, picking up trash.
One of the male tourists from Australia commented that although there was a lot of trash, nobody was doing anything.
The beach was not as nice or beautiful as it should be.
He felt so sad to see such a gorgeous place littered with so much trash.
Thus, he and his friends decided to grab a few trash bags and clean it all up. 2 A man passing by decided to video their good deed and put it on the internet.
It was unclear where the rest of the group was from, but they were most likely traveling together.
One local woman commented on being embarrassed that tourists were cleaning up their beach.
Another mentioned that it was actually the natives who brought food and drinks then left trash all along the island.

questions.stem: Why did one of the male tourists feel sad?

options.text: One of his friends was caught littering.
Other tourists refused to join in the cleanup.
The beautiful beach was spoiled with lots of trash.
The kilometer-long beach was practically deserted.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：He felt so sad to see such a gorgeous place littered with so much trash.信号：feel sad 与题干同词直接命中 。答案句直接出现题干里的 He felt so sad，紧跟其后的 to see such a gorgeous place littered with so much tras…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：A 项借用录音里的 his friends 一词，但原文只说他和朋友一起去捡垃圾，从没说‘朋友被抓乱扔垃圾’，是把出现过的原词拼成一个录音根本没说的情节。 借用原文：Yesterday two male and three female tourists were spotted walking the kilometer-long beach
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：录音说的是‘nobody was doing anything’（没人去管这些垃圾），并非‘其他游客拒绝加入清理’；‘refused to join in’这一情节录音从未出现，属凭空捏造。
optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：D 项盗用录音里的 kilometer-long beach，却说海滩‘practically deserted（几乎空无一人）’；而录音强调的是海滩满是垃圾、不够美，与‘空无一人’语义不符，方向反了。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（such a gorgeous place littered with so much trash ↔ The beautiful beach was spoiled with lots of trash 同义改写：美景被垃圾糟蹋）

questions.evidenceText: He felt so sad to see such a gorgeous place littered with so much trash.

questions.stem: Who put the good deed video on the internet?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：A man passing by decided to video their good deed and put it on the internet.信号：动作 put it on the internet 与题干同动作 。答案句出现与题干同样的动作 put it on the internet，前面的主语 A man passing by 就是施动者；听到题干里的关键…

optionAnalysis.B: 张冠李戴：B 项盗用录音里的 One local woman，但这位本地女子做的是‘评论说自己很尴尬’，并非上传视频；把别人做的事安到她头上，属人物错位。 借用原文：they were most likely traveling together
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：录音通篇没出现‘beach authorities（海滩管理方）’这个角色，上传视频的也不是任何官方机构，属凭空捏造的身份。
optionAnalysis.D: 张冠李戴：D 项盗用录音里的‘游客’，游客确实是事件主角、在捡垃圾，但发视频到网上的是路过男子而非游客中的某人；把上传动作错记到游客身上。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（A man passing by ↔ A passerby 短语压缩成单词）

questions.evidenceText: A man passing by decided to video their good deed and put it on the internet.

questions.stem: Why did one local woman say she was embarrassed?

options.text: The tourists' good deed was not noticed by the locals.
Some natives were selling poor-quality food to tourists.
The number of tourists to the beach is on a steady decline.
It was tourists not natives who were cleaning up the beach.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：One local woman commented on being embarrassed that tourists were cleaning up their beach.信号：embarrassed that 直接引出原因 。答案句出现题干同词 embarrassed，紧跟的 that tourists were cleaning up their beach 由 that 直接引出尴尬的…

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：A 项说‘游客善举没被本地人注意到’，但录音里本地女子明明注意到了才会尴尬，路人还拍了视频，恰恰说明被注意到了；‘not noticed’与录音事实相反。 借用原文：it was actually the natives who brought food and drinks then left trash all along the island
optionAnalysis.B: 偷换概念：B 项盗用录音里的 food and drinks，但原文是说本地人‘带来食物饮料后留下垃圾’，绝非‘卖劣质食物给游客’；把‘带来食物乱丢垃圾’偷换成‘卖劣质食物’。
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：录音通篇没提‘游客数量在持续下降’这一信息，本题谈的是清理海滩与尴尬，与游客增减无关，属凭空捏造的全新话题。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（that tourists were cleaning up their beach ↔ It was tourists not natives who were cleaning up the beach 补出隐含对照：游客而非本地人）

questions.evidenceText: One local woman commented on being embarrassed that tourists were cleaning up their beach.

transcript.text: W: Hello Benjamin, Dan and I will be going for a run along the canal Saturday morning. Would you like to join us?
transcript.zh: W: 你好 Benjamin,我和 Dan 周六早上要沿着运河跑步。你想一起来吗?

transcript.text: M: I'd love to, but I hurt my ankle last weekend playing football with work colleagues.
transcript.zh: M: 我很想去,但我上周末和同事踢足球时伤了脚踝。

transcript.text: W: Oh dear, is it serious?
transcript.zh: W: 哎呀,严重吗?

transcript.text: M: No, not at all. I landed badly during a fall and twisted it a little, but it's no big deal. It's just a little swollen and I should be fine for next Saturday if you still want to go for a jog then.
transcript.zh: M: 不,一点也不严重。我摔倒的时候落地不太好,扭了一下,但不是什么大事。只是有点肿,下周六应该就没事了,如果你那时候还想去慢跑的话。

transcript.text: W: I won't be here next Saturday. I'm going to the zoo.
transcript.zh: W: 我下周六不在这儿。我要去动物园。

transcript.text: M: The zoo?
transcript.zh: M: 动物园?

transcript.text: W: Yeah. My little nephew turns six, and he loves the zoo, so the whole family is going.
transcript.zh: W: 对。我小侄子要过六岁生日了,他很喜欢动物园,所以全家人都要去。

transcript.text: M: Oh, okay then. I haven't been to a zoo since I was a kid.
transcript.zh: M: 哦,好吧。我从小时候起就没去过动物园了。

transcript.text: W: They are nowhere near as popular as they used to be when we were children. I personally feel sorry for the poor animals stuck in cages, but there's no denying they are fun and educational for children.
transcript.zh: W: 动物园远不像我们小时候那么受欢迎了。我个人觉得那些被关在笼子里的可怜动物很可怜,但不可否认的是,它们对孩子们来说既有趣又有教育意义。

transcript.text: M: Do you know if Dan will be around next Saturday?
transcript.zh: M: 你知道 Dan 下周六有空吗?

transcript.text: W: Yeah, I think he will. Just send him a text message. He's always keen on physical activities.
transcript.zh: W: 嗯,我觉得他应该有空。给他发个短信吧。他总是很热衷于体育活动。

transcript.text: M: That's true. Dan is extremely fit and healthy. He goes to the gym most days, plus tennis two or three times a week.
transcript.zh: M: 没错。Dan 身体特别好。他几乎每天都去健身房,再加上每周打两三次网球。

transcript.text: W: So, what have you been doing to stay busy while you've had that swollen ankle?
transcript.zh: W: 那么,你脚踝肿的这段时间都在忙些什么呢?

transcript.text: M: I've been catching up on some reading. I was given three books over Christmas, and I'm only now getting around to reading them.
transcript.zh: M: 我一直在补看一些书。圣诞节的时候收到了三本书,现在才开始读。

questions.stem: Why can't the man go for a run Saturday morning?

options.text: He has to play football with workmates.
He has got some books to read.
He is going to visit a friend.
He is physically unfit for it.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：I'd love to, but I hurt my ankle last weekend playing football with work colleagues.信号：转折 but 后才是真理由 。男士先说 I'd love to（很想去）是客套，紧跟的 but 才转出真正原因——I hurt my ankle，所以答案句落在 but 之后。

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：选项 He has to play football with workmates. 把原文里的 playing football with work colleagues 原词搬来，但原文是说"踢球时受了伤"、不是"周六要去踢球"，听到 football 就选会落进陷阱。 借用原文：I've been catching up on some reading
optionAnalysis.B: 张冠李戴：选项 He has got some books to read. 说的是他后面提到的读书 I've been catching up on some reading，那是第11题的内容，与"为何不能去跑步"无关，属张冠李戴。
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：选项 He is going to visit a friend. 在对话里根本没出现，男士不能去跑步的理由是脚伤，不是去看朋友，纯属编造。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（I hurt my ankle ↔ He is physically unfit for it. 具体伤情概括成"身体不适合"）

questions.evidenceText: I'd love to, but I hurt my ankle last weekend playing football with work colleagues.

questions.stem: Why is the woman's whole family going to the zoo next Saturday?

options.text: To teach kids about animal protection.
To learn how popular zoos could be.
To see some rare animals in cages.
To give her little nephew a treat.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P7）：My little nephew turns six, and he loves the zoo, so the whole family is going.信号：因果 so 引出去的原因 。so the whole family is going 里的 so 把前因"小侄子过六岁生日、又喜欢动物园"和后果"全家去"连起来，so 之前就是"为什么去"的答案。

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：选项 To teach kids about animal protection. 借了女士后面说的 they are fun and educational for children 里的 educational，但原文只说动物园对孩子有趣又有教育意义，从没说全家去是为了"教孩子动物保护"，是把原词拔高到原文没说的目的。 借用原文：They are nowhere near as popular as they used to be
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：选项 To learn how popular zoos could be. 套用了 They are nowhere near as popular as they used to be 里的 popular，但那只是女士顺口评论动物园不如从前受欢迎，绝不是全家去的目的。 借用原文：the poor animals stuck in cages
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：选项 To see some rare animals in cages. 借了 the poor animals stuck in cages 里的 cages，但原文是女士同情笼中动物，没说去看"珍稀"动物，rare 更是凭空添加。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（My little nephew turns six, and he loves the zoo ↔ To give her little nephew a treat. 为侄子庆生=给侄子一份开心）

questions.evidenceText: My little nephew turns six, and he loves the zoo, so the whole family is going.

questions.stem: What do we learn about Dan from the man's description?

options.text: He is keen on extreme sports.
He coaches tennis players every week.
He spends most of his time in the gym.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P12）：Dan is extremely fit and healthy. He goes to the gym most days, plus tennis two or three times a week.信号：直接给出对 Dan 的总评 。男士 Dan is extremely fit and healthy 是对 Dan 的直接定性评价，后面 gym、tennis 都是佐证，这句总评就是答案句。

optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：选项 He is keen on extreme sports. 把 Dan 的运动夸大为"极限运动"，原文只说他常去健身房、打网球，从没提 extreme sports，属无中生有。
optionAnalysis.C: 偷换概念：选项 He coaches tennis players every week. 搬来原文的 tennis 和 a week，但原文是 Dan 自己"打"网球 plus tennis two or three times a week，不是"教"网球选手，把"打"偷换成"教"。 借用原文：He goes to the gym most days
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：选项 He spends most of his time in the gym. 借了 He goes to the gym most days 里的 gym 和 most，但原文是"多数日子去健身房"，选项偷偷改成"把大部分时间花在健身房"，频率被夸大成时长。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（Dan is extremely fit and healthy ↔ He enjoys excellent health. extremely fit and healthy = excellent health）

questions.evidenceText: Dan is extremely fit and healthy. He goes to the gym most days, plus tennis two or three times a week.

questions.stem: What has the man been doing since last weekend?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P14）：I've been catching up on some reading. I was given three books over Christmas, and I'm only now getting around to reading them.信号：I've been doing 直接应答 。女士问他脚伤期间在干嘛，男士直接以 I've been catching up on some reading 应答，被问者的这句应答就是答案句，与题干时态对应。

transcript.text: W: Our guest on today's Book Talk is John Black, the author of the new bestseller, Retire Early.
transcript.zh: W: 我们今天《书谈》节目的嘉宾是 John Black，新晋畅销书《提前退休》的作者。

transcript.text: M: Thanks for having me on the show, Lisa.
transcript.zh: M: 谢谢邀请我来节目，Lisa。

transcript.text: W: John, your book is getting a lot of attention, partly because you write that most people can retire by 40. Is that realistic?
transcript.zh: W: John，你的书正受到很多关注，部分原因是你在书中写到大多数人可以在 40 岁退休。这现实吗？

transcript.text: M: Definitely. When researching this book, I interviewed hundreds of people who retired by 40.
transcript.zh: M: 绝对现实。在研究这本书时，我采访了数百位在 40 岁前退休的人。

transcript.text: W: Okay, but how much money does a person need to retire? I've read articles recommending one million dollars as a good figure for retirement.
transcript.zh: W: 好吧，但是一个人需要多少钱才能退休？我读过一些文章推荐一百万美元作为退休的合适数字。

transcript.text: M: While most financial planners do give numbers, I don't think that's useful, as people are living in different areas with different costs of living, and have different needs and wants, which is why I suggest that people aim for financial independence.
transcript.zh: M: 虽然大多数理财规划师确实会给出具体数字，但我认为那没什么用，因为人们生活在不同地区，生活成本不同，需求和期望也不同，所以我建议人们以财务独立为目标。

transcript.text: W: What do you mean by financial independence?
transcript.zh: W: 你说的财务独立是什么意思？

transcript.text: M: Having investment income that's greater than monthly expenses.
transcript.zh: M: 就是投资收入大于月度开销。

transcript.text: W: That sounds risky to me. What if an accident happens or you get ill and need medical treatment? Shouldn't people have extra cash for emergencies?
transcript.zh: W: 这在我看来有点冒险。如果发生意外或者生病需要医疗怎么办？人们不应该留些额外现金以备不时之需吗？

transcript.text: M: Too many people spend their lives working on jobs they hate because they're afraid, so I counsel people to take risks. Retirement doesn't have to be permanent, and if people need to, they can go back to work.
transcript.zh: M: 太多人因为恐惧而一辈子做着自己讨厌的工作，所以我建议人们去冒险。退休不一定是永久的，如果需要，人们可以重返工作。

transcript.text: W: But it's not always easy to get back into the workforce after an extended absence.
transcript.zh: W: 但是长时间离开职场后再回去并不总是那么容易。

transcript.text: M: True, but if you keep current with your skills, you will be attracted to employers.
transcript.zh: M: 确实，但如果你保持技能更新，你会对雇主有吸引力的。

transcript.text: W: Maybe, but how can anyone save enough to retire by 40 when most people can't retire at 60?
transcript.zh: W: 也许吧，但大多数人 60 岁都退不了休，怎么可能有人能存够钱在 40 岁退休呢？

transcript.text: M: Simple, by cutting housing, food, and transport expenses, and investing half your monthly income.
transcript.zh: M: 很简单，削减住房、食物和交通开支，然后把月收入的一半用于投资。

transcript.text: W: That sounds impossible.
transcript.zh: W: 这听起来不可能。

transcript.text: M: I admit it's difficult, but it has worked for thousands.
transcript.zh: M: 我承认很难，但对成千上万的人确实有效。

transcript.text: New research from America studies the role that the presence of individuals from different social or racial groups has in influencing consumers' food choices. This research found college students were more likely to choose healthy food in the presence of an observer of a different race, as opposed to an observer from their own race. The same was true when they were with someone from a different university, compared to someone from their own. Researchers say this was because participants anticipated more negative judgment from an outsider group. In contrast, they felt less judged by members of their own group.
transcript.zh: 来自美国的新研究探讨了来自不同社会或种族群体的个体的存在对消费者食物选择的影响作用。该研究发现,与同种族观察者在场相比,大学生在不同种族观察者在场时更有可能选择健康食品。当他们与来自不同大学的人在一起时,情况也是如此,而不是与来自自己大学的人在一起时。研究人员表示,这是因为参与者预期会受到外部群体更多的负面评判。相比之下,他们感到受到自己群体成员的评判较少。

transcript.text: In one experiment, participants were offered the choice between candy and fruit as a snack. When in the presence of an unknown student from their own university, only 12 percent of students selected the healthier option. However, this number was 31 percent when in the presence of an unknown student from another university. Other experiments showed similar results based on racial group.
transcript.zh: 在一项实验中,参与者可以选择糖果或水果作为零食。当与一名来自自己大学的陌生学生在场时,只有12%的学生选择了更健康的选项。然而,当与一名来自另一所大学的陌生学生在场时,这一数字为31%。其他基于种族群体的实验显示了类似的结果。

transcript.text: What's the reason for this pattern? The study found that people feel judged to a larger extent by members of other groups. Because of this, they strategically use healthy food choices to make a positive impression. There have been many attempts to help consumers make healthier choices, but consumers often struggle to maintain a healthy diet. This research finds that one way to promote a healthy diet could be to advertise the social benefits of healthy choices.
transcript.zh: 这种模式的原因是什么?该研究发现,人们感到在更大程度上受到其他群体成员的评判。因此,他们策略性地使用健康食品选择来留下积极印象。已经有许多尝试帮助消费者做出更健康的选择,但消费者往往难以保持健康饮食。该研究发现,促进健康饮食的一种方法可能是宣传健康选择的社会益处。

options.text: They tended to be easily anticipated by those belonging to their own race.
They tended to be arbitrarily judged by individuals of opposing groups.
They were readily shared among members of the same social or racial group.
They were influenced by the presence of someone from an outsider group.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：This research found college students were more likely to choose healthy food in the presence of an observer of a different race, as opposed to an observer from their own race.信号：结论标志词 found 。录音 This research found 直接亮出研究结论，found 后面跟的就是研究发现，这是篇章交代核心结论的标志，听到 found/showed 这类词就知道答案句来了。

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：A 用了录音后文 participants anticipated more negative judgment 里的 anticipated 一词，但把它扭成易被同族人预料，与研究发现毫无关系，是听到原词就想选的陷阱。 借用原文：they felt less judged by members of their own group
optionAnalysis.B: 偷换概念：B 说食物选择被对立群体的个人任意评判，借了录音 they felt less judged by members of their own group 的 judge 概念，但研究发现的是选择被在场者影响，不是选择本身被评判，偷换了概念。 借用原文：they felt less judged by members of their own group
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：C 说食物选择在同族群体内易被共享，但录音 they felt less judged by members of their own group 讲的是同族在场时人感觉评判更少、影响更小，根本没说共享选择，且方向与研究重点（外群体才带来改变）相反。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（in the presence of an observer of a different race ↔ influenced by the presence of someone from an outsider group 下位换上位）

transcript.text: For college students under pressure, a dog may be the best stress fighter around, according to the finding of a recent study. "It's a really powerful finding," said Patricia Pendry, who led the study. "Universities are doing a lot of great work trying to help students succeed academically, especially those who may be at risk due to a history of mental health issues or academic and learning issues. This study shows that traditional stress management approaches aren't as effective for this population compared with programs that focus on providing opportunities to interact with therapy dogs."
transcript.zh: 根据最近一项研究的发现，对于压力之下的大学生来说，狗可能是最好的压力克星。领导这项研究的Patricia Pendry说："这是一个非常有力的发现。大学正在做大量出色的工作来帮助学生在学业上取得成功，尤其是那些可能因心理健康问题史或学业和学习问题而处于风险中的学生。这项研究表明，传统的压力管理方法对这一群体的效果不如那些专注于提供与治疗犬互动机会的项目。"

transcript.text: The researchers measured executive functioning in the students involved in the study. Executive function is a term for the skills one needs to plan, organize, motivate, concentrate and memorize. These are skills students need to succeed in college. The researchers found that students who were most at risk had the most improvements in executive functioning after interacting with therapy dogs. These results remained when researchers followed up six weeks later.
transcript.zh: 研究人员测量了参与研究的学生的执行功能。执行功能是指一个人计划、组织、激励、集中注意力和记忆所需的技能。这些是学生在大学取得成功所需要的技能。研究人员发现,风险最高的学生在与治疗犬互动后,执行功能改善最大。当研究人员在六周后进行随访时,这些结果仍然保持。

transcript.text: Many universities provide academic stress management programs and workshops. These are traditionally very similar to college classes. They often talk about ways to get more sleep, set goals, or manage stress or anxiety. Pendry acknowledges that these are really important topics and these workshops help typical students succeed. But they're less helpful for struggling students. Pendry believes those students may experience the programs as another lecture and feel even more stressed.
transcript.zh: 许多大学提供学业压力管理项目和研讨会。这些传统上与大学课程非常相似。它们通常讨论如何获得更多睡眠、设定目标或管理压力或焦虑的方法。Pendry承认这些是非常重要的话题,这些研讨会帮助典型学生取得成功。但它们对挣扎中的学生帮助较小。Pendry认为,那些学生可能会将这些项目体验为又一次讲座,并感到更加紧张。

transcript.text: Taking risks in business does not mean going into business blindly and then expecting great results. On the contrary, taking risks in entrepreneurship involves careful planning and hard work. Nobody can really be sure if risks will be met with success, no matter how calculated they may be. But this should not stop you from taking risks, as risks are necessary if you want your business to succeed.
transcript.zh: 在商业中冒险并不意味着盲目创业然后期待巨大的成果。相反,创业中的冒险涉及周密的计划和艰苦的工作。无论风险计算得多么仔细,没有人能真正确定风险是否会获得成功。但这不应该阻止你冒险,因为如果你想让企业成功,冒险是必要的。

transcript.text: Some risks may not work out, but an optimistic risk-taker will always look at failure as an opportunity to learn. The willingness to experiment with new ideas is key to business growth. As the old saying goes, "Nothing ventured, nothing gained." Failure will teach you how to think and plan strategically. But just remember that not all risks are good ones, and when you fail, learn from it and move forward.
transcript.zh: 有些风险可能不会成功,但乐观的冒险者总是将失败视为学习的机会。愿意尝试新想法是企业成长的关键。正如老话所说,"不入虎穴,焉得虎子。"失败会教你如何进行战略思考和规划。但要记住,并非所有风险都是好的,当你失败时,要从中吸取教训并继续前进。

transcript.text: Since most people tend to avoid risk, businesses that are brave enough to take risks already have a competitive advantage. They are the ones setting the standard with new ideas, fresh offers and bold inventions. Risk-takers are best at adapting in difficult times. Simply put, when most individuals stay away from risk, it means less competition for risk-takers. We don't know if you'll achieve what these risk-takers have achieved. But for as long as you want to stay safe, and for as long as you are content with where your business is right now, you will never find out.
transcript.zh: 由于大多数人倾向于规避风险,那些勇于冒险的企业已经拥有了竞争优势。他们用新想法、新颖的产品和大胆的发明树立标准。冒险者最善于在困难时期适应。简单地说,当大多数人远离风险时,这意味着冒险者面临的竞争更少。我们不知道你是否能取得这些冒险者所取得的成就。但只要你想保持安全,只要你满足于企业目前的状况,你就永远不会知道答案。

Exercising for just 10 minutes a week is linked to a longer life, according to a new study published in The British Journal of Sports Medicine.

The study was based on data from more than 88,000 U.S. adults who 29______ in the National Health Interview Survey between 1997 and 2008.

Contrary to some research that has found an 30______ limit to the amount of exercise that is healthy, the researchers found that there was 31______ no limit to the longevity(长寿) benefits of exercise. Even the small group of people who got 10 times the amount of exercise recommended by the federal government had a 46% lower 32______ of death than the least active group.

Still, observational studies like this one cannot prove cause and effect; they can only find 33______ . The researchers also were not able to 34______ for certain lifestyle factors that could affect lifespan, including dietary habits and changes in physical activity over time. Despite these 35______ , the study's results are yet another indication of the power of physical activity, even in small amounts.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Earlier this year, scientists warned that one in six animal species could go extinct(灭绝的) due to climate change. Could the same thing happen to our crops and other foodstuffs too?

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: It's clear that farmers in many parts of the world are going to find things harder in the coming decades. Last week, BBC Future explored one scientist's efforts to help crops cope with the increased probability of droughts. By using the genes from resurrection(复活) plants, Jill Farrant of the University of Cape Town is exploring whether she can design crops to survive for much longer periods without water.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: But if we can't find ways to protect other foods, will they survive climate change? Fortunately, there is some good news on this front. Despite alarmist headlines about "foods that are going extinct," there is no evidence that major food types like beans, chocolate, wine, corn or wheat will cease to exist.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: But that doesn't mean it's all good news for future food. We will probably have to change where we grow certain crops, as some regions get too hot. The disadvantage, obviously, is that local farmers will suffer under this situation. And some people may struggle to get the same access to certain foods. "Even if overall food production may be unaffected, food security can still be impacted," says Margaret Walsh, a scientist at the US Department of Agriculture's Climate Change Program Office. In other words, even if a certain food is still grown on some corner of the Earth, it doesn't mean that everyone will continue to have the same degree of access as today.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Overall, the yields of many foods, from staples to life-enhancing extras such as coffee and chocolate, will likely be impacted by climate change too. How those decreases will be felt will depend on the degree of warming and the crop in question, but in general, "anything over about 30℃ is very bad for crops," says Wolfram Schlenker, an associate professor of international and public affairs at Columbia University. For example, statistical studies that he and a colleague built of corn and soybean(大豆) production in the US show a steep decline after crossing the 30℃ temperature threshold(临界点).

paragraphs.label: F

"What's common to all studies is the finding that extreme heat is damaging to crop growth, although exact cutoffs vary by crop," Schlenker says. paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Under current conditions, about 4% of the world's croplands experience drought in any given year, but by the end of the century those conditions are forecasted to jump to about 18% per year. Some studies indicate that horticulture crops—generally, everything besides staples—may be impacted most severely, largely because they tend to be confined to a smaller geographic area. paragraphs.label: I

paragraphs.label: L

"We've seen profound changes in the last decades in what we eat largely as a result of international trade, and I think that trend toward more diversification will continue," M Jarvis says. 中国政府十分重视人民的健康饮食(diet)。通过大力提倡健康饮食，人们对合理营养增进健康的重要性有了更加深刻的认识。"吃得安全、吃得营养、吃得健康"是人民对美好生活的基本需要，是提升人民幸福感的必然要求，也为食品产业的发展提供了新机遇。目前，各级政府都在采取多种举措确保人民饮食健康，推进健康中国的建设。

【参考译文】
The Chinese government attaches great importance to people's healthy diet. Through the vigorous promotion of a healthy diet, people have come to better understand the importance of balanced nutrition in improving health. Eating safely, nutritiously and healthily is a basic need of the people for a better life, an inevitable requirement for enhancing their sense of happiness, and also offers new opportunities for the development of the food industry. At present, governments at all levels are taking various measures to ensure people's dietary health and promote the building of a Healthy China.
